title: Comparing Classification and Feature Learning by Analyzing Their Loss Functions in Normalized Spaces with Different Scale Factors
abstract: arXiv:2611.07741v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Classification and feature learning are two closely interrelated fundamental tasks. Feature learning in supervised settings is typically achieved by training classification models, under the common assumption that higher classification accuracy implies better feature quality. In this paper, we first point out that classification accuracy reflects the sample-wise local properties of a model on a dataset, whereas feature learning aims to learn features with good dataset-level global properties, such as intra-class compactness and inter-class separability. From the first principle of feature learning, we redesign the binary cross-entropy (BCE) loss, a counterpart of the cross-entropy (CE) loss used in classification. Then, in normalized feature space, we analyze the minima of the BCE and CE losses and show that both can lead to neural collapse, where sample features from different classes become maximally compact and maximally separated. Mo

translated_title: 通过在不同尺度因子的归一化空间中分析损失函数来比较分类与特征学习
translated_abstract: 分类和特征学习是两个密切相关的基本任务。在监督设置下，特征学习通常通过训练分类模型来实现，普遍的假设是更高的分类准确率意味着更好的特征质量。在本文中，我们首先指出分类准确率反映的是模型在数据集上的样本级局部性质，而特征学习旨在学习具有良好数据集级全局性质的特征，例如类内紧凑性和类间可分性。从特征学习的第一性原理出发，我们重新设计了二元交叉熵损失，它是分类中使用的交叉熵损失的对应版本。随后，在归一化特征空间中，我们分析了BCE和CE损失的极小值，并证明两者都可以导致神经坍缩现象，即来自不同类别的样本特征变得最大程度地紧凑且最大程度地分离。
tldr: 本文指出分类准确率反映的是样本级局部性质，而特征学习追求的是数据集级全局性质，并从第一性原理重新设计BCE损失，在归一化特征空间中分析其与CE损失的极小值，证明两者均可导致神经坍缩。
en_tdlr: This paper distinguishes classification (sample-wise local properties) from feature learning (dataset-level global properties), redesigns the BCE loss from the first principles of feature learning, and proves in normalized feature space that both the BCE and CE losses can lead to neural collapse.
